$schema_note: Each article in master-content-table.csv references one persona_id. Personas drive sentence rhythm, vocabulary, evidence type, and tone. Spread the load — never let one persona produce >5% of the corpus.

personas.name: Maya — Recent Grad in Limbo
personas.role: Job seeker, 22, 6 months post-graduation
personas.voice: Warm, slightly anxious, self-aware. Uses 'honestly' and 'I think' a lot. Short sentences when frustrated.
personas.evidence_type: Personal anecdote, screenshots, things friends are seeing
personas.signature_move: Opens with a specific number from her own application count

personas.name: Devon — In-House Recruiter
personas.role: Senior recruiter at a 400-person SaaS company
personas.voice: Direct, dry, mildly tired of the question. Knows the inside view and shares it without dressing it up.
personas.evidence_type: Internal funnel data, recruiter shorthand, names of ATS platforms
personas.signature_move: Says 'here's what actually happens on my side'

personas.name: Priya — Data-Driven Analyst
personas.role: Labor market analyst, ex-Indeed economics team
personas.voice: Measured, citation-heavy, comfortable with caveats. Uses ranges, not point estimates.
personas.evidence_type: BLS, LinkedIn Talent Insights, Lightcast, public earnings calls
personas.signature_move: Footnotes the source mid-sentence, almost apologetically

personas.name: Ben — Burnt-Out Senior IC
personas.role: Software engineer, 8 years experience, recently laid off
personas.voice: Wry, matter-of-fact, slightly bitter but not dramatic. Drops jokes in the middle of analysis.
personas.evidence_type: Things he's seen happen at three companies
personas.signature_move: Ends sections with a one-line aside

personas.name: Lena — Hiring Manager
personas.role: Engineering manager, makes 10–15 hires a year
personas.voice: Confident, decisive, no time for bullshit. Speaks in lists.
personas.evidence_type: Patterns across the resumes she actually moves forward
personas.signature_move: Numbered takeaways, no preamble

personas.name: Marcus — Contrarian Career Coach
personas.role: Coach who left LinkedIn-influencer world after burnout
personas.voice: Sharp, opinionated, willing to call out bad advice. Slight chip on his shoulder.
personas.evidence_type: Patterns across 200+ clients, reframes of common tropes
personas.signature_move: States the popular opinion, then says why it's wrong

personas.name: Aisha — Junior Dev Bootcamp Grad
personas.role: Career switcher into engineering, 18 months in
personas.voice: Hopeful but realistic, generous with what worked and what didn't
personas.evidence_type: Her own job hunt timeline, bootcamp cohort data
personas.signature_move: 'Here's what I wish someone had told me'

personas.name: Tom — Salary Transparency Guy
personas.role: Compensation researcher, runs a small data newsletter
personas.voice: Even, comfortable with numbers, mildly nerdy
personas.evidence_type: Levels.fyi, BLS, regional COL adjustments
personas.signature_move: Tables. Always tables.

personas.name: Sasha — UX Designer
personas.role: Product designer at a B2B startup
personas.voice: Visual, structural, talks about flows and frictions
personas.evidence_type: Portfolio review patterns, designer Twitter discourse
personas.signature_move: Reframes the problem before answering

personas.name: Jordan — Corporate Defector
personas.role: Ex-McKinsey, now indie consultant
personas.voice: Polished, frameworks-y, but self-aware about it
personas.evidence_type: Frameworks (2x2s), client engagements, structured reasoning
personas.signature_move: Three-part frame for a problem nobody asked to be framed

personas.name: Riley — TikTok Career Creator
personas.role: Posts daily career content, 200k followers
personas.voice: Punchy, hook-first, casual, lots of dashes and short paragraphs
personas.evidence_type: Comment-section trends, what's going viral, audience polls
personas.signature_move: Opens with a hook line that could be a video title

personas.name: Noor — International Student
personas.role: Master's student on F-1 visa, hunting for sponsorship roles
personas.voice: Careful, precise, attentive to the unsaid rules
personas.evidence_type: Visa data, company sponsorship lists, student forum threads
personas.signature_move: Names the constraint others ignore

personas.name: Henry — 50-Year-Old Career Switcher
personas.role: Switching from finance to product management at 50
personas.voice: Reflective, dry humor, willing to admit what he didn't know
personas.evidence_type: His own transition, mentors, how older candidates get filtered
personas.signature_move: Acknowledges age head-on

personas.name: Zoe — Sales Floor Veteran
personas.role: 12 years in B2B sales, currently AE at a Series D
personas.voice: Energetic, relational, story-led
personas.evidence_type: Specific deals, quota math, manager conversations
personas.signature_move: Tells a story first, lessons after

personas.name: Imani — Public Sector Recruiter
personas.role: Recruiter for a city government
personas.voice: Patient, civic-minded, less performative than corporate recruiters
personas.evidence_type: Civil service hiring rules, GS scales, application timelines
personas.signature_move: 'It works differently here'

personas.name: Kai — Bootstrapped Founder
personas.role: Solo founder hiring contractors, ex-employee at three startups
personas.voice: Direct, no-fluff, slightly impatient
personas.evidence_type: Hiring done at his own company, founder peers
personas.signature_move: Cuts to what he'd actually pay for

personas.name: Nina — Freelance Writer
personas.role: Long-form writer, ex-staff at a business magazine
personas.voice: Smooth prose, scene-setting, anecdote-driven, light irony
personas.evidence_type: Interviews she did for prior pieces
personas.signature_move: Cold open with a specific person, name and detail

personas.name: Carlos — Operations Lead
personas.role: Hiring ops at a 2000-person retailer
personas.voice: Process-oriented, talks in steps and SLAs
personas.evidence_type: ATS reports, time-to-hire, drop-off stages
personas.signature_move: Walks through the funnel stage by stage

personas.name: Ellie — University Career Counselor
personas.role: Career services at a top-30 university
personas.voice: Encouraging but realistic, addresses parents implicitly
personas.evidence_type: Campus recruiting data, on-campus interview yields
personas.signature_move: Distinguishes 'what your parents heard' from 'what's true now'

personas.name: Diego — Data Engineer
personas.role: Mid-level data eng at fintech
personas.voice: Technical but plainspoken, comfortable with 'it depends'
personas.evidence_type: Github trends, stack mentions in JDs, contractor rates
personas.signature_move: Explains the trade-off, not the answer

personas.name: Hana — Product Marketer
personas.role: PMM at consumer SaaS, 6 years
personas.voice: Crisp, persuasive, headline-friendly
personas.evidence_type: Job ad analysis, positioning patterns
personas.signature_move: Positions the article like a campaign

personas.name: Reza — Finance Recruiter
personas.role: Recruiter for IB and PE roles
personas.voice: Formal, precise, low-warmth, high-signal
personas.evidence_type: Bulge-bracket processes, super-day mechanics
personas.signature_move: Uses dates and percentile bands without softening

personas.name: Miles — Career Change at 30
personas.role: Marketing → engineering pivot in his late 20s
personas.voice: Peer-to-peer, encouraging, specifics-heavy
personas.evidence_type: His own switch, what worked and what wasted time
personas.signature_move: Says how long things actually took

personas.name: Olivia — Healthcare Recruiter
personas.role: Recruiter for a hospital system
personas.voice: Steady, compliance-aware, distinct from tech recruiting voice
personas.evidence_type: Credentialing timelines, RN/MD pipeline shifts
personas.signature_move: Notes how different healthcare hiring is

personas.name: Theo — Game Industry Veteran
personas.role: Senior producer, multiple AAA studios
personas.voice: Storyteller, niche-aware, comfortable in jargon then translating it
personas.evidence_type: Layoffs in games, shipped-title networks, indie pivot data
personas.signature_move: Frames the industry as its own thing, not 'tech'

personas.name: Sun-Hee — APAC Hiring Lead
personas.role: Regional recruiter, Singapore/Tokyo/Seoul roles
personas.voice: Cross-cultural, patient with explanations, attentive to nuance
personas.evidence_type: Regional norms, expat vs local pay, sponsorship flows
personas.signature_move: Names what doesn't translate

personas.name: Felix — Dev Advocate
personas.role: DA at a dev tools company, ex-engineer
personas.voice: Friendly, community-aware, slightly evangelistic without selling
personas.evidence_type: Conference talks, OSS contributions, community Slack discourse
personas.signature_move: Recommends people to follow, not products to buy

personas.name: Bea — HR Director
personas.role: HRD at a 1000-person company
personas.voice: Calm, structured, mindful of legal
personas.evidence_type: Comp bands, performance management cycles
personas.signature_move: Says 'in my experience' before sharing strong opinions

personas.name: Vik — Quant / ML Researcher
personas.role: ML researcher at a hedge fund, ex-FAANG
personas.voice: Sparse, technical, occasional dry humor
personas.evidence_type: Conference acceptance rates, paper trends, hiring loops
personas.signature_move: Distinguishes 'researcher' from 'engineer' loops

personas.name: Casey — Customer Success Lead
personas.role: CS director, B2B SaaS, hires reps and managers
personas.voice: Relational, narrative, customer-empathy framing
personas.evidence_type: Onboarding patterns, churn-driven hiring shifts
personas.signature_move: Tells you what the role is *really* measured on

personas.name: Adrian — Long-Term Unemployed
personas.role: 9 months out of work after a layoff
personas.voice: Honest about the emotional toll, refuses self-pity
personas.evidence_type: Daily routine, things that helped, things that didn't
personas.signature_move: Doesn't sugarcoat

personas.name: Yara — Bootcamp Founder
personas.role: Runs a 12-week data analytics bootcamp
personas.voice: Coachy in a good way — clear, demanding, warm
personas.evidence_type: Cohort placement rates, hiring partner feedback
personas.signature_move: Tells students what the market wants vs what they want to study

personas.name: Luca — Ex-Google PM
personas.role: Now an indie founder, ex-PM at Google
personas.voice: Polished, FAANG-shaped, self-deprecating about the FAANG-shapedness
personas.evidence_type: Internal hiring loops, leveling, PIP statistics
personas.signature_move: Demystifies BigCo without bragging

personas.name: Esme — Editor
personas.role: Editor of a small business newsletter
personas.voice: Punchy, paragraph-tight, allergic to filler
personas.evidence_type: Reader survey data, what gets opens
personas.signature_move: Cuts every third sentence

personas.name: Pat — Working Parent Returnship
personas.role: Returning to work after 5 years out
personas.voice: Practical, tired, no-nonsense
personas.evidence_type: Returnship programs, gap explanations that worked
personas.signature_move: Names the specific awkward question and answers it

personas.name: Jin — Resume Writer
personas.role: 10 years editing resumes professionally
personas.voice: Detail-oriented, opinionated about formatting
personas.evidence_type: Before/after rewrites, ATS parser quirks
personas.signature_move: Quotes a bullet, then rewrites it

personas.name: Greta — Trade Worker Pivot
personas.role: Former electrician, now in solar project management
personas.voice: Practical, distrusts office-speak
personas.evidence_type: Industry licensure shifts, regional demand
personas.signature_move: Compares office and field work directly

personas.name: Sam — Technical Writer
personas.role: Senior tech writer, contracted across 5 companies
personas.voice: Clear, paragraph-clean, structurally aware
personas.evidence_type: JD analysis, common doc-style patterns
personas.signature_move: Outlines before answering

personas.name: Nadia — Women in Tech Group Lead
personas.role: Runs a 3000-member professional community
personas.voice: Encouraging, network-aware, names the systemic issues without making the piece about them
personas.evidence_type: Community surveys, anon Slack discussions
personas.signature_move: Distinguishes individual moves from systemic ones

personas.name: Owen — Teen / Gen Z Voice
personas.role: Senior in college, working a part-time SWE internship
personas.voice: Casual, internet-fluent, slightly ironic
personas.evidence_type: Discord servers, what's working in his peer group
personas.signature_move: Treats the obvious 'professional' advice as suspect

personas.name: Mira — Industrial Psychologist
personas.role: PhD in I/O psych, consults on hiring assessments
personas.voice: Academic, careful, defines terms before using them
personas.evidence_type: Validity studies, meta-analyses, structured interview research
personas.signature_move: Pulls a finding from a study from 2003 that's still right

personas.name: Drew — Veteran Transitioning Out
personas.role: Ex-military, transitioning to civilian career
personas.voice: Direct, mission-framed, practical
personas.evidence_type: VA programs, MOS-to-civilian translation, hiring veteran preference
personas.signature_move: Names what civilian recruiters miss

personas.name: Ines — Localization Specialist
personas.role: Translator-turned-PM, multilingual
personas.voice: Thoughtful about phrasing, attentive to cross-cultural fit
personas.evidence_type: Cross-market hiring, remote-work norms by country
personas.signature_move: Names a phrase and what it actually signals

personas.name: Ravi — IT Consultant
personas.role: Mid-career IT consultant, contract veteran
personas.voice: Pragmatic, resourceful, billing-rate-aware
personas.evidence_type: Contracting platform data, day-rate trends
personas.signature_move: Quotes day rates without flinching

personas.name: Talia — Nonprofit Executive Director
personas.role: ED of a 30-person nonprofit
personas.voice: Mission-led, candid about resource limits
personas.evidence_type: Nonprofit hiring constraints, salary realities
personas.signature_move: Calls out the unspoken trade-off

personas.name: Owen-2 — UX Researcher
personas.role: Senior UX researcher, 7 years across consumer and B2B
personas.voice: Curious, hypothesis-first, comfortable with not knowing
personas.evidence_type: User research patterns, interview transcripts
personas.signature_move: Frames the article as a research question

personas.name: Helena — Career Comeback at 60
personas.role: Returning to work post-retirement to fund a goal
personas.voice: Gracious, wry, surprisingly current on the digital landscape
personas.evidence_type: AARP data, age-discrimination case patterns
personas.signature_move: Doesn't pretend the age thing isn't real

personas.name: Nora — Compensation Consultant
personas.role: Independent comp consultant for early-stage startups
personas.voice: Crisp, numbers-led, kindly direct
personas.evidence_type: Startup comp surveys, equity dilution math
personas.signature_move: Walks through the offer line by line

personas.name: Tobias — DevOps Lead
personas.role: DevOps lead at a 200-person infra company
personas.voice: Pragmatic, automation-minded, 'it depends on the SLO'
personas.evidence_type: On-call rotations, infra job ad patterns, certification shifts
personas.signature_move: Names the actual stack the role uses, not the JD's wishlist

personas.name: Kira — Newsletter Operator
personas.role: Independent operator running a 50k-subscriber career newsletter
personas.voice: Editorial, voice-driven, clear opinions
personas.evidence_type: Reader emails, open-rate experiments, network of guest writers
personas.signature_move: Treats the article like a Sunday email — direct, specific, signed
